The firm combines quantitative research, advanced technology, and systematic trading to identify market opportunities and develop profitable trading strategies.

Role: Quantitative Researcher

  • Master's or PhD in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Financial Engineering, or a related discipline.

Iowa INSIGHT is a statewide initiative that will produce scientific evidence needed to understand how environmental exposures affect human health — from the air Iowans breathe to the water they drink. The program will work to identify environmental factors contributing to Iowa’s high cancer rates and other adverse health problems, including maternal and newborn health, reproductive health, and neurodevelopmental disorders. The Assistant Research Scientists will lead research initiatives centered on environmental monitoring and biomonitoring, while contributing to a vibrant team of researchers at CHEEC that includes research staff, as well as graduate and undergraduate student researchers. This is a specified term position. This position is not eligible for University sponsorship for employment authorization. Key Responsibilities: Initiate research design and methodology. Originate design, research conduct, and coordination. Maintain laboratory equipment as needed. Develop hypotheses to be tested and select methodology. Work independently on moderately complex research tasks with oversight by Faculty or Principal Investigator. Provide routine operation and maintenance of instrumentation involved in the analysis of environmental and biological samples. Contribute to documentation of equipment and procedures. Perform advanced data analysis techniques. Analyze data for relevance and data integrity. Develop new applications of existing data analysis techniques. Compare results of scientific investigations to previously published work. Develop methods for analysis of complex environmental samples, including water, air and heterogeneous media, and/or biospecimen samples (e.g., whole blood, serum, urine, breast milk). Prepare and submit manuscripts for publication. Demonstrate strong publication record. May contribute to public data archives or other resources; e.g., software, models, or on-line tools to support scientific research. Prepare and submit publications (e.g., lead and/or corresponding author) in peer-reviewed scientific journals. Present results in departmental seminars and at professional meetings. Contribute to new or continuing research grant proposals to obtain funding for research activities. May serve as co-PI on grants or proposals. Contribute to research proposals and funding agency reports. May write research proposals to obtain independent funding as PI. Select and purchase equipment as needed. Supervise adherence to safety and compliance guidelines when necessary. Provide service to the scientific community, University and General Public. May serve on departmental or University committees. Consult and collaborate with the research community. May organize outreach efforts in alliance with funding sources. May serve as a session chair or organize sessions at professional meetings. Mentor graduate students. May provide functional and/ or administrative supervision for staff. Provide direction, assignments, feedback, coaching and counseling to assure outcomes are achieved. We pride ourselves on producing ethical, globally aware engineers whose work makes the world safer and more efficient. As a center of innovation and discovery, the College of Engineering is committed to improving the quality of life for our Iowa community, as well as for people across the United States and around the world. We uphold the values of respect, community, and collaboration in all our endeavors, fostering a welcoming and respectful environment where members are valued and supported. Joining our team means becoming part of a supportive environment that values work-life balance and personal well-being. The University of Iowa offers a comprehensive benefits package, including health and wellness resources, dual career support, and opportunities for professional development. Prior experience and significant expertise with analysis of environmental and/or biospecimen samples via liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Demonstrated expertise in the routine operation and maintenance of instrumentation involved in the analysis of environmental and biological samples. Prior experience in developing and maintaining appropriate QA/QC standards and protocols associated with laboratory analysis of environmental and biological standards. Prior experience managing complex data flows, including translating data into reports that can be shared with stakeholder groups. full_description:
Who We Are

Roboflow is building the visual cortex for AGI.

Every day, millions of developers and half of the Fortune 100 use Roboflow to count cells to accelerate cancer research, improve construction site safety, digitize floor plans, preserve coral reef populations, guide drone flight, and much more.

We have built the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. We're supported by great customers and investors, having raised over $100 million from Google Ventures, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, Y Combinator, and more.

Roboflow Labs is our applied research unit. We train our own open models (RF-DETR). We build our own benchmarks grounded in real enterprise use cases (RF100-VL). And we partner with frontier labs to deliver the training data they need to advance the capabilities that drive the most value back to our customers.

Behind all of it is a global network of millions of Roboflow developers who have annotated billions of images and videos to date, as well as a proven enterprise business that is exploding as AI traverses the physical economy.

What You'll Do

As a Research Scientist at Roboflow Labs, you'll sit at the intersection of our benchmarks, our models, and the researchers at frontier labs who buy our data: running failure analyses that show exactly where a model breaks on real-world tasks, turning those findings into dataset and evaluation specifications, and validating that the data we ship actually moves the numbers. You'll publish, extend RF100-VL and the benchmarks that follow it, and help set the research agenda for a team whose work is grounded in millions of real deployments rather than fabricated test sets.

  • Design datasets, evaluations, and RL environments that target measurable gaps in frontier vision-language, multi-modal, robotics, and coding models

  • Run structured failure analyses on partner labs' models against Roboflow's real-world task distribution and write the remediation specs that say what data will close each gap

  • Own the research behind new benchmarks that we publish.

  • Validate data quality empirically — fine-tune, ablate, and measure so that every dataset we sell comes with evidence it works

  • Contribute to Roboflow's open models (RF-DETR and successors) and represent Labs within the research community

  • Work directly with research scientists at frontier labs as a technical peer, translating their model roadmaps into concrete data programs

Who You Are

You are a researcher who wants to see your work turn into data that ships. You have high agency and a bias toward action.

  • PhD or equivalent research experience in computer vision, multi-modal learning, machine learning, or a closely related field, with a track record of published work or shipped research

  • Hands-on experience with post-training: fine-tuning, RL, evaluation design, or data curation for large models

  • Strong engineering fundamentals — you write the code for your own experiments and can hand it to an engineer to productionize

  • Clear written communication; you can explain a failure mode to a lab researcher and a data spec to an annotator

  • Nice to have: experience at a frontier lab or as a data/evaluation partner to one; experience with vision-language models, robotics learning, or agentic coding evaluations

Where You'll Work

Roboflow is a fully distributed company with hubs in San Francisco, New York City, Singapore, and Brazil. Roboflow Labs works in person in San Francisco. We host full company retreats twice per year.

What You'll Receive

The target compensation for this role is $250,000 – $450,000 base salary commensurate with experience as well as equity in the company. Total cash comp is expected to scale significantly with growth of Roboflow Labs.

In addition, we offer generous perks and benefits. Below are some of the highlights:

  • Generous stipends covering travel, productivity, tools, meals, and office.

  • Up to 100% of your health insurance costs covered.

  • Unlimited PTO - with an annual 2 week minimum.

  • 12 weeks parental leave

Not sure if this is you?

We want a diverse, global team with a broad range of experience and perspectives. We carefully consider every application and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

Learn More About Us

At Roboflow, we believe great ideas come from everywhere, and everyone. We’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. About Generalist

At Generalist, we are on a mission to build general intelligence for the physical world and make it useful to everyone. We believe the industries and homes of the future will depend on humans and machines working together in new ways. Robots can help us build more and get more done.

We build embodied foundation models, starting with a focus on dexterity. This requires advancing the frontiers of data, models, and hardware, to enable robots to intelligently interact with the physical world.

The company embraces both large-scale AI and robotics as core to its DNA. Our team of researchers, roboticists, and company builders come from OpenAI, Boston Dynamics, Google DeepMind, and other frontier labs—with a track record of shipping AI breakthroughs. Before Generalist, we pioneered large embodied multimodal models and vision-language-action models (PaLM-E, RT-2, Gemini Robotics), launched and scaled ChatGPT and GPT-4 to hundreds of millions of users, engineered the foundations of autonomous driving, built next-generation robots (Atlas, Spot, Stretch) and pushed the limits of what they can do (from parkour to manipulation, and testing robustness).

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

About the Role

Applied Scientists own the mastery of new frontier model capabilities. This includes developing post-training recipes for learning a wide range of dexterous tasks — from pushing the frontiers of science lab automation, to generalizing manufacturing and warehouse logistics, to designing open-ended evaluations that challenge what the models can do, and more. You are responsible for hill-climbing broad sets of manipulation capabilities until they are robust, general, and reusable across multiple applications. This role is a hybrid of research, engineering, and operations, and we expect excellence in all three areas.

This is an empirical, model science-first role. You will define what "good" looks like for a capability, build the evaluations that measure it, run experiments across model variants and data recipes, analyze the results, and drive the post-training loop. You will leverage post-training, data, task design, and rigorous experimentation, to compound model capabilities: anything mastered for one application can become a strength of the foundation model for entire industries.

You'll be responsible for:

  • Owning end-to-end improvement of target capabilities, from baseline performance to mastery

  • Designing task suites and evaluation protocols that faithfully capture what research, science partners, and customers need, and that generalize beyond any single deployment

  • Coordinating data collection, training and fine-tuning models, sweeping data mixtures and configurations, and orchestrating large-scale evaluations

  • Running rigorous experimental analysis across model variants — isolating variables, quantifying statistical confidence, and diagnosing failure modes from rollout data

  • Using the stack in new ways rather than redesigning it — and when a capability is fundamentally restricted, you'll work with the pretraining and post-training teams to improve the model

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are comfortable with data analysis at scale: slicing roll out logs, computing metrics, visualizing results, and investigating what happened and why

  • Care deeply about evaluation, benchmarking, and failure analysis — and are continuously diligent in the face of seemingly repetitive, but subtly changing task evaluations

  • Enjoy rapid iteration with real-world feedback loops, and are willing to get hands-on with robots and physical task setups when the experiment demands it

  • Are motivated by making capabilities work for real applications

  • Can communicate findings clearly to both research teams and partner-facing teams

  • Have a strong background in machine learning and/or robot learning (e.g. a PhD in a relevant area)
